newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Historic site looted, vandalised in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Historic site looted, vandalised in Albania.

text.p: World-famous ruins at Butrint have been looted and vandalised as part of widespread civil unrest sweeping southern Albania, a Ministry of Culture official said at the site on Monday.
UNESCO and British Lords Rothschild and Sainsbury have funded work at the 40-acre site where Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Venetian ruins were excavated in recent years.

"There has been both theft and vandalism, which is an outrage since Butrint is the most important archaeological site in Albania and of great international significance," said Telemak Llahana from the Institute of Cultural Monuments.
"The continuity of our culture since 800 BC is in evidence here as at no other location. Now we are missing some statues and the archaeologists are unable to work."
Butrint occupies a spectacular isthmus in southern Albania looking across the Ionian sea to Corfu.
Ministry of Culture staff abandoned Butrint following widespread lawlessness sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes in Albania.
Doors to the museum and archaeological storerooms in a partially restored Venetian fortress overlooking the site have been smashed in recent days and some statues stolen, Llhana told Reuters.
Glass display cases in the museum were shattered and some statues had been toppled. Boxes and plastic bags with bits of pottery were strewn across the floor of the main storeroom.
"There was some monetary value to the pieces which were been taken, but they were mostly of value to Albania as part of the nation's heritage," Llhana said.
Butrint, which has about 25,000 visitors a year, has figured prominently in various schemes to boost tourism in Albania in recent years.
"The storeroom was full of statues and they are gone," said Wilma Goudappel, an Australian who lives in Albania and who has been bringing tour groups to the site since 1991.
"Butrint never seems to come into its own. There is a lot of international interest in the site but unfortunately the Albanians never quite seem to get their act together."
